analysis: Both changed files are test-only. MiMoV26EncodedMediaIngressTests.swift line 560 changes the pattern match from `ingested.video` to `ingested.video.source`. This tracks an API shape change in MediaIngest.decodeVideo, where the result is now a wrapper struct around a source enum. The test still asserts the memory-backed path and fails on a plaintext or URL video path, so it keeps checking that data-URI video stays in memory and does not use temp files (T-050). ProviderLoopNativeMiMoLifetimeTests.swift line 41 updates the NativeFaultPeerModel `prepare` signature to take `state` and `prefill` parameters, matching an upstream LanguageModel protocol change. That peer model is an admission-only test double that returns `.tokens(input.text)`, so it has no production attack surface. No production source, trust boundary, key handling, cache or attestation code is modified in the supplied units. The new `.source` API and the PrefillParameters semantics live in non-supplied files. Whether the production change keeps the memory-backed ownership and managed-media reservation guarantees is a question for the units that change those files, not for these tests. The e39dd1a731d99925:0 unit was metadata only. I identified no security regression or threat-model gap from these test edits.
